Again, on November 22, The Indian Express reported that the Uttar Pradesh BJP had instructed its workers to focus on Form 6 additions in the SSR to ensure inclusion of names of individuals eligible to be voters but left out during the SIR for some reason. The workers, outsourced through the contractor, had begun their strike on November 18. They claimed that they were underpaid and that no Provident Fund (PF) or Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) contributions had been deducted or deposited for about three months. They also claimed that they were made to work extra hours and that their wages were paid in instalments, with half paid earlier and the balance released after Diwali. The absence of ESIC cover meant that one worker who sustained a chest injury on duty was meeting the cost of treatment himself. Another suffered a nail puncture to the foot and had received no benefit. The workers claimed that several letters to the Registrar and the Vice-Chancellor (VC) had drawn no effective response. items.title: Why actor Sreejith TR was convicted in POCSO case: A closer look at the verdict
items.summary: A Thrissur court on Monday, November 23, sentenced Malayalam film actor Sreejith TR to one year of rigorous imprisonment in a sexual harassment case involving two minor girls. The two girls were subjected to sexual harassment by Sreejith on the porch of their apartment complex in July 2022. The court also imposed a fine of Rs 50,000 on him. The Special Fast Track Court-II, Thrissur, presided over by Judge Remya Menon, found Sreejith guilty under Section 11(i) read with Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, which deals with sexual harassment of a child and prescribes punishment for it, and Section 509 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), which criminalises words or acts intended to insult a woman's modesty. However, the court applied Section 42 of the POCSO Act, under which the law prescribing the harsher punishment applies when an act is an offence under both laws. The court imposed the sentence only under the POCSO Act and did not award a separate sentence under Section 509 IPC. items.title: NCDRC holds LIC liable for its agent's fraud after premium paid by customer diverted, misutilised
items.summary: The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) recently held the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) vicariously liable for the misutilization and diversion of the premiums paid by a customer to one of its agents [Goldstar Diamond Pvt. Ltd. v Life Insurance Corporation of India Ltd. & Ors.] . A coram of President Justice AP Sahi and Member Bharatkumar Pandya ruled that the LIC was deficient in service for allowing premiums paid towards renewal of existing insurance policies to be diverted towards issuing new policies, causing financial loss to the policyholder. It added that LIC cannot escape liability merely because its agent had committed fraud, particularly when the premiums had been credited to and retained by the Corporation. "We therefore cannot segregate or divorce this relationship of principal and agent of the LIC with the OP-2 (LIC insurance agent), keeping in view the provisions of Section 182 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872. items.title: ITAT upholds tax benefits for Tata Sons on loans taken to fund investments in group companies

Judicial Member Amit Shukla and Accountant Member GM Doss on October 29 held that the activities of Tata Sons extended beyond merely holding shares to earn dividends and that interest paid on borrowings for its investment-holding business qualified for deduction under the Income Tax Act. “ The assessee’s activities therefore extend beyond the passive holding of shares for the receipt of dividend ,” the ITAT observed. The dispute concerned the financial year 2013-14, during which Tata Sons incurred interest expenditure of ₹1,498.71 crore and other borrowing costs of ₹35.35 crore. During the same period, the company earned ₹4,387.19 crore in dividends and ₹453.29 crore in brand subscription fees. The Income Tax Department refused to allow Tata Sons to deduct interest paid on its borrowings from its taxable income on the ground that investing in group companies was not its business.
